study type: Observational comparative study with repeated measures
exposure: Mode of birth (vaginal delivery vs. cesarean delivery)
cohort: The study participants included 22 nulligravid control women and 29 postpartum women (20-40 years old), of whom 19 had vaginal births and 13 had cesarean sections.
finding: Postpartum women exhibited deficits in trunk flexor strength, fatigability, and steadiness compared to nulligravid controls, indicating incomplete musculoskeletal recovery up to 26 weeks postpartum.
mod_finding: At 8 weeks postpartum, women with cesarean delivery were 59% more fatigable than those with vaginal delivery, but this difference was no longer present at 26 weeks postpartum.
cross-section timing: Measurements were taken at 8-10 weeks and 24-26 weeks postpartum for the postpartum group, and 16-18 weeks apart for control women.
